question.problem:
The graph below shows a section of the function $y=\dfrac{1}{3}\cot{(x+C)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} <            C <            \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ what is the value of $C?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14256901/assets/140eb5ba37908504b1976eefb29cf3515569314b28bc7a752d3d705e27702a58.png)
question.worked_solution:
The constant $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function $y=\dfrac 1 3\cot x.$

From the graph, we see that the given curve shifted **left** by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ units. So, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\frac 1 3\cot\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right).
$$

Therefore, $C = \dfrac{1}{2}.$
